1595 reserved Linux BlueZ/HID stale-bond acceptance

Generation performs no device action. All cases start not_run. This plan covers
host @HOST@, controller @ADAPTER@, peripheral serial @SERIAL@ at @ADDRESS@,
using @PROFILE@. Run the other HID transport with its own actual peripheral and
plan. A fake D-Bus peer, synthetic input directory or connection status alone
cannot establish physical recovery. Preserve the first failure and every retry.

Reservation and identity

1. Reserve this Linux bench and peripheral with their owner. Retain an independent
   wired console and wired management path; the tested HID must not be the only
   keyboard or mouse controlling recovery. Use a console with no application that
   treats the chosen test buttons as destructive actions. Stop only bench-owned
   viewers that grab the test input device. Do not stop unrelated input services.
   Inventory must include real OS release, kernel, BlueZ version, controller model/
   firmware/USB identity, peripheral serial/model/firmware and its selected host
   slot. Record unknown firmware explicitly; do not infer it from a product name.

2. Confirm the generated controller_address_on_target command returns @ADAPTER@.
   Re-read the adapter index after reboot. Verify the Agent's selected adapter,
   including any WENDY_BT_ADAPTER override, agrees with this controller. If adapter
   selection is ambiguous, stop and prepare a documented dedicated bench setup.
   Do not repoint another user's controller. Inspect actual Agent service PID and
   /proc/PID/exe, hash the running executable, and compare with inventory. Record
   source revision, installed binary hash, uname -a, /etc/os-release, bluetoothd
   --version and boot ID. Do not install a candidate as an implicit plan step.

3. Confirm target Address and its original Paired/Trusted/Connected values with
   the generated busctl commands. Confirm UUIDs contain the transport actually
   used: 00001812-0000-1000-8000-00805f9b34fb for LE HID, or
   00001124-0000-1000-8000-00805f9b34fb for classic HID. Save original-state and
   owner-reviewed recovery records before pairing. A rotating/unresolved address
   that cannot be tied to the same physical identity is an unavailable setup.

4. Review peripheral-bond-reset.json against the actual vendor instructions.
   Its steps must clear only this peripheral's reserved host slot/bond while the
   host retains its bond. The expected confirmation must be physically observable.
   There is no generic reset button sequence. If this model has no documented
   peripheral-only method, keep bond-loss and both recovery cases pending. Do not
   delete /var/lib/bluetooth, call RemoveDevice/forget or reset the host adapter to
   manufacture a stale-host state. Those operations remove the precondition.

Baseline with real input

5. Start a fresh case directory, UTC timeline and full Agent journal capture.
   Confirm btmon, busctl, dbus-monitor, stdbuf, timeout and evtest are installed and their --help matches
   the commands. Confirm the reserved account already has the needed observation
   access; sudo -n must fail rather than wait for credentials. Run baseline_pair on the management host. This bounded command
   requests pairing and trust for only @ADDRESS@; owner authorization is required
   for executing this generated procedure. Require Paired=true, Trusted=true,
   Connected=true, the expected HID UUID and a matching real kernel input uniq.
   Copy bluez-input-observer.py to the reserved board, verify its source hash and
   run input_registry_on_target there. It reads only actual /sys/class/input;
   it does not create a fake input device or read another peripheral's events.

6. Pick an event node reported beneath the matching input device. Verify the
   node's sysfs ancestry and uniq before and after every capture, because event
   numbers can change when HID reconnects. Set OBSERVED_EVENT_NODE to that exact
   /dev/input/eventN. On the reserved board, from the new case directory:
     sudo -n timeout --signal=INT --kill-after=3s 20s evtest "$OBSERVED_EVENT_NODE" > input-events.txt 2>&1
   Use capture mode, with no --grab and no injection tool. During the interval,
   press/release only the reserved peripheral's safe controls in this fresh order:
     @CHALLENGE@
   Run nonce: @NONCE@. Save a timestamped observer note linking the physical
   actions to the device serial and capture. Require actual EV_KEY press/release
   transitions matching the order, not merely the capability header or static
   key state. A timeout 124 ending the configured observation window is expected;
   it is never sufficient acceptance without the fresh events. Other early errors
   or a capture killed after the grace period leave input acceptance incomplete.

Create and prove the mismatch

7. Run disconnect_target and require Connected=false and disappearance of the
   matching input device. Wait at most ten seconds. If a stale kernel input node
   remains, preserve evidence and stop; it could falsely satisfy input readiness.
   Require host Paired=true and Trusted=true. Record the exact target properties
   and, where authorized, metadata and SHA256 of that target's BlueZ bond record.
   Never print/copy its key material or the complete Bluetooth state directory.

8. Execute only the exact vendor recipe on the peripheral's reserved slot, within
   @RESET_SECONDS@ seconds. Record the physical confirmation, serial/slot and UTC
   time. Put this same peripheral into its documented pairing/advertising mode.
   Recheck host Paired=true and Trusted=true WITHOUT forgetting/re-pairing first.
   Confirm no matching input node and no successful automatic reconnect occurred.
   The host still having a record plus a verified peripheral-only reset establishes
   the mismatch. A guessed reset, changed peripheral address/slot or a routine
   disconnect is not stale-bond evidence. Restore the healthy baseline and repeat
   the setup if auto-reconnect consumed it before the measured command.

Measured repair

9. Use separate terminals: start target_methods_on_target with both stdout/stderr
   redirected to a fresh dbus-methods.txt, start the bounded controller trace,
   start input_registry_on_target in a fresh directory, then run
   repair_preserving_live_trust on the management host. Save the complete command
   exit/output and correlated Agent journal. The command explicitly sets trust=false
   to prove that a previously live Trusted=true survives RemoveDevice and re-pairing.
   It still requests pair=true. Do not issue a second connect while it runs.
   Before and after the measured connect, run target_paired and require its
   Properties.Get call in dbus-methods.txt. A denied/terminated monitor or missing
   boundary calls leaves method observation incomplete. Require the successful
   repair to show Adapter1.RemoveDevice with the exact target object path argument
   and Device1.Pair on the target path. This is the positive control for the same
   method filters used in the no-pair case; retain method sender IDs and timestamps.
   An unrelated client's intervention makes attribution inconclusive.

10. Classify the actual trigger separately; do not force both branches from one run:
    - Key-error recovery requires an observed key/authentication failure and the
      production 'Connect failed with a stale-bond error' message, followed by
      removal, rediscovery, fresh pairing and successful connection. RF loss or
      a generic timeout is not evidence of this branch.
    - Hollow-HID recovery requires initial BlueZ Connected=true with no matching
      kernel input device, then production's unchanged eight-second input wait
      and 'HID device connected but produced no input device' message. Require
      the subsequent stale removal/fresh pair and real input arrival. Use the
      input registry timeline and HCI/Agent timestamps; do not create a fake node
      or shorten the production timeout. If this device instead reports an
      authentication error, record that branch and leave hollow-HID not_run.
    For each observed branch, require the bounded command to exit 0, the production
    'Re-paired Bluetooth device after dropping stale bond' event, Paired=true,
    Trusted=true and Connected=true for the same identity, plus the fresh input
    challenge from step 6 after repair. A successful RPC without real input fails.
    Record actual elapsed time; the 60-second CLI bound is an upper failure bound,
    not a performance acceptance target. Keep a nonreproducible branch pending.

No implicit bond removal and reconnect

11. From a healthy baseline, recreate the peripheral-only mismatch exactly as in
    steps 7–8. Start a new target_methods_on_target trace using the same already-verified
    filters. Capture target properties, HCI, input registry and Agent journal,
    then run no_pair_control. Require target_paired Properties.Get boundary calls
    before and after the complete command interval, with no monitor error or gap. This explicitly sets pair=false/trust=false. Require
    no target RemoveDevice or Pair method at all during that bounded interval.
    Check RemoveDevice's object-path argument, since its method lives on the
    adapter. Mere absence of a successful repair log cannot prove this. If D-Bus
    monitoring is unavailable, keep this no-removal proof pending. The call may fail or report a
    direct connection, because this mode deliberately does not authorize bond
    removal; it must not be counted as repaired HID unless actual events appear.
    If the peripheral itself initiates fresh pairing, retain that trace and mark
    the no-repair case inconclusive. Restore using the explicit pair=true command
    and verify fresh input again before continuing. Never leave a known broken
    bond as a successful test cleanup.

12. Once repaired, disconnect only this target, power-cycle only the reserved
    peripheral using its normal operation, and explicitly connect it again.
    Require the same physical identity/profile and a new real input challenge
    within 60 seconds. Existing device paths or old event logs cannot satisfy this.
    Repeat each observed stale trigger from a newly established healthy baseline;
    write each attempt into a new evidence directory without overwriting failures.

Bounds, recovery and acceptance

13. Observation commands own only their foreground child processes. Let timeout
    finish and confirm no test btmon/evtest/observer remains. Never use broad pkill.
    Controller traces contain sensitive Bluetooth traffic; restrict access and
    publish only redacted evidence. Preserve the full original traces privately.
    Export the exact measured Agent journal interval using the actual service unit:
      sudo -n journalctl -u "$OBSERVED_AGENT_UNIT" --since "$CASE_START_UTC" --until "$CASE_END_UTC" --no-pager
    On a timed-out RPC, preserve evidence and inspect the same target through the
    independent console before any next operation. Do not restart system BlueZ or
    wipe bonds as an automatic retry. Use only the owner-reviewed recovery record.

14. Re-establish the original paired/trusted/connection state from recovery.txt.
    If the bench originally had no bond, remove only the test target through the
    owner-approved cleanup recipe; do not clear other host slots or devices.
    If it had a bond, fresh re-pairing may replace its key, so verify actual input
    and owner acceptance rather than claiming that an old key was restored.
    Recheck an unrelated reserved control peripheral where available and confirm
    no other bond/controller was changed. Account for any necessary repair.

15. Fill evidence.json per case with exact source/binary/kernel/BlueZ/profile
    identities, first-failure logs, mismatch proof, elapsed times, HCI/Input/Agent
    observations and cleanup result. The other HID transport stays not_run until
    a separate exact-target plan runs. An independent reviewer must accept the
    physical identity and input evidence. Generation, portable tests and synthetic
    D-Bus success cannot mark these hardware cases passed.

Tool references:

https://manpages.debian.org/bookworm/evtest/evtest.1.en.html
